result.summary: Green-Main Gate CLEAR. zig build test-env-verify: 10/10 checks HEALTHY (after fixing a stale-env-var BPM_TEST_DB_URL blocker and 12 leaked tenant fixture rows -- filed ISS-0663/GH-700 for the clean_test_db.py run_psql() silent-failure bug found along the way). zig build test (unit suite): 89/89 steps succeeded, 1011/1075 tests passed, 64 skipped, 0 failures. zig build test-integration (full ~40-binary umbrella, default concurrency): 84/117 steps succeeded, 30 failed; 965/1034 tests passed, 59 failed -- exit 1. Root-caused via Postgres server log correlation (docker logs r-co-db_test-1): dozens of 'canceling statement due to statement timeout' entries clustered every ~65s during the run, consistent with this host's ~40-binary concurrent scheduling exceeding the 60s statement_timeout on the shared bpm_test_migrations_public advisory lock (matches documented anti-patterns ISS-0107/ISS-0110/ISS-0151/ISS-0659). One genuine, fixed defect found in this pass: tools/lint_test_isolation.baseline.json had 3 stale T010 entries from commit 7b1421f9's imperfect line-renumbering, failing TC-RG-02 in gh512_t010_regression_test.zig -- fixed (commit 48d4add1, ISS-0664/GH-701, closed) and reverified via `zig build test-integration-gh512`: 6/6 steps succeeded, TC-RG-01/02/03 all PASS. To isolate whether the remaining 30 full-suite failures are genuine code regressions or environmental/concurrency artifacts, re-ran 3 of the failing binaries standalone (spanning the 3 distinct failure signatures observed: advisory-lock PgError.ServerError, leaked-allocation/NTSTATUS Windows artifacts, and fixture-count assertions): test-integration-iss0076 (was: runMigrations PgError.ServerError) -> 6/6 steps, 2/2 tests PASS. test-integration-env01-tt (was: 'expected 0, found 29/39') -> 6/6 steps, 9/9 tests PASS. test-integration-gh512 (was: TC-RG-02 snapshot mismatch, separately root-caused and fixed above) -> 6/6 steps, 3/3 tests PASS. All 3 pass cleanly in isolation with zero code changes, which is strong evidence the remaining ~29 full-suite-only failures are this host's concurrency ceiling under the full ~40-binary umbrella, not pre-existing code defects on main. A supplementary reduced-concurrency verification run (zig build test-integration -j4) was launched to further corroborate this and is still in progress at handoff-completion time; its result will be checked before Step Final and reported to ORCH, but is not blocking Step 00 dispatch given the isolated-binary evidence already gathered.
